2027-01-28.title: Saint Thomas Aquinas, Priest and Doctor of the Church
readings: Let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith
Such are the people who seek your face, O Lord
Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket?
2027-01-28.verse: He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed, and not on the lampstand?
theo: Hebrews tells us that we have “confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus, by the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain (that is, through his flesh)”. So: “let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith… Let us hold fast to the confession of our hope without wavering… And let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds, not neglecting to meet together.” Faith, hope and love, lived in community, especially in the Sunday assembly.

Jesus asks: “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket?” The light of the Gospel is meant to shine. Few have let it shine more brightly than St Thomas Aquinas, the Dominican friar whose mind served the faith with clarity and humility. He taught that faith and reason are two lights from the one God. Near the end of his life, after an experience at Mass, he stopped writing, saying that all he had written seemed like straw compared with what he had seen. He wrote the hymns we sing before the Blessed Sacrament: Pange lingua, Tantum ergo, Adoro te devote. His learning ended in adoration.

2027-01-28.prayer: O God, who made Saint Thomas Aquinas outstanding in his zeal for holiness and his study of sacred doctrine, grant us, we pray, that we may understand what he taught and imitate what he accomplished. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: St Thomas taught that in the Eucharist Christ is present whole and entire, by the change the Church calls transubstantiation. His hymns still lead us to adore.

2027-01-28.question: Is my faith a lamp on the stand or under a basket?

family.explain: Jesus says we do not hide a lamp under a basket; we put it where everyone can see. Our faith should shine too!
family.intention: We pray for students and teachers, through St Thomas Aquinas.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family let our faith shine?”

illus: A medical student in Thrissur struggled with doubts after a science lecture. Her chaplain gave her a page from St Thomas Aquinas on faith and reason. She said: I had thought I must choose between my microscope and my rosary. Thomas taught me that both are gifts of the same God.

pm.open: Lord, give us minds that seek you and hearts that adore you, like St Thomas Aquinas. Amen.
share: Let us approach with a true heart (Hebrews 10:22). How do I come to God?
Not neglecting to meet together (Hebrews 10:25). Do I value Sunday Mass?
A lamp… on the lampstand (Mark 4:21). Where should my faith shine?
pm.resp: Lord, let your light shine in us.
interc: For theologians and teachers of the faith.
For all who adore the Blessed Sacrament.
For our group, that we may encourage one another.
pm.close: Father, you gave St Thomas wisdom and humility. Enlighten our minds and kindle our love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says that through the blood of Jesus we have confidence to enter the sanctuary, by the new and living way that he opened for us (Hebrews 10:19–20). So let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith.

It adds: let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some (Hebrews 10:24–25). Faith is lived together, especially at Sunday Mass.

Jesus says a lamp is not put under a basket but on the lampstand (Mark 4:21). St Thomas Aquinas let the light of faith shine through his mind. He showed that faith and reason are friends, two lights from one God.
Yet his learning ended in adoration. He wrote the hymns we sing before the Blessed Sacrament. Let us study our faith and kneel before the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, St Thomas Aquinas was very clever, but he loved Jesus in the Eucharist most of all. Let us learn about our faith and pray to Jesus!

q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

concl: Faith is confident, communal and luminous.
Like Thomas, let our study lead us to adore.
